blocks.text: 1. Additive Attention
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785445882323-928348060.png

Scaled Dot-Product Attention, the previous topic, refined the dot product scoring approach with a simple scaling fix. Additive Attention offers an alternative scoring approach using a genuinely small learned network instead, explored throughout this topic.

It works by combining Query and Key through addition, then passing the result through its own dedicated small network, a genuinely different mathematical strategy covered throughout the rest of this topic.
2. Recapping The Dot Product Approach
This connects back to the scoring step, already covered throughout Dot-Product Attention and Scaled Dot-Product Attention. Both prior topics genuinely used a dot product to compute relevance scores.
Additive Attention genuinely takes a fundamentally different, more flexible mathematical approach, explored in full depth throughout the rest of this topic.
3. The Core Idea
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785445882324-710821663.png

Additive Attention's genuinely core idea connects back to combining Query and Key, already covered generally in Query, Key, and Value. Add the Query and Key vectors together, rather than genuinely multiplying them via a dot product.
This genuinely different combination method, already covered in this section, gives this entire technique its own distinctive name and mathematical character.

blocks.text: 4. The Small Learned Network
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785445882324-818397944.png
This connects back to fully connected layers, already covered in Network Architecture. The genuinely summed vector then genuinely passes through a small, dedicated fully connected layer.

This produces the genuinely final relevance score, a genuinely learned computation rather than a fixed formula, directly contrasting with the parameter-free dot product already covered in the previous two topics.
5. The Activation Function Involved
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785445882325-427948003.png
This connects back to Tanh, already covered in the Activation Functions module. This small network genuinely typically applies Tanh before producing its own final score.

This directly reuses that earlier activation function for a genuinely new, specific purpose, adding the genuine non-linearity already covered as Tanh's own general role throughout that earlier module.
6. More Parameters Than Dot-Product Attention
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785445882325-383239253.png

This connects back to the simplicity benefit, already covered in Dot-Product Attention. Additive Attention genuinely needs its own additional learned weights for that small network, already covered in this topic.

This is a genuinely direct, honest tradeoff against the parameter-free scoring already covered there, echoing the same kind of tradeoff already covered generally throughout this course between simplicity and flexibility.

blocks.text: 7. Why It Might Learn Richer Scores

A genuinely potential advantage connects back to more non-linearity, already covered generally in VGG. A genuinely learned, non-linear scoring function can in principle capture genuinely richer relationships than a simple dot product.

This genuinely potential benefit, already covered in this section, is the theoretical motivation behind Additive Attention's own design, even though it comes with the genuine tradeoffs already covered earlier in this topic.
8. The Computational Cost Tradeoff
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785445882325-388448885.png
This connects back to computational efficiency, already covered in Dot-Product Attention. Additive Attention genuinely costs more computation than the simple dot product already covered there.

This is a genuinely real, practical reason Scaled Dot-Product Attention became the more widely adopted default, already covered in the previous topic, favoring efficiency over Additive Attention's own theoretical flexibility.

blocks.text: 9. Recognizing When Additive Attention Is Genuinely Still Relevant

blocks.alt: Recognizing When Additive Attention Is Genuinely Still Relevant
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785445882325-767470809.png

This connects back to genuinely lower-dimensional Query and Key vectors, where its extra cost matters less. Additive Attention, already covered in this topic, can genuinely remain a reasonable choice there.

Understanding this earlier historical approach, already covered, is another genuine case, offering genuinely useful context for appreciating why Scaled Dot-Product Attention, already covered, became the standard default instead.
10. Worked Example
The example below directly demonstrates computing an Additive Attention score, contrasting its structure against the dot product approach already covered in the previous two topics.

code.content:
import numpy as np

rng = np.random.RandomState(42)
hidden_size = 4

query = rng.normal(size=hidden_size)
key = rng.normal(size=hidden_size)

# already covered as the small learned network in this topic
W_combine = rng.normal(size=(hidden_size, hidden_size)) * 0.1
v_score = rng.normal(size=hidden_size) * 0.1  # already covered as producing the final score

def additive_attention_score(query, key, W_combine, v_score):
    combined = query + key  # already covered as the core idea in this topic
    activated = np.tanh(W_combine @ combined)  # already covered as the activation function involved
    return np.dot(v_score, activated)  # already covered as the small learned network's final output

def dot_product_score(query, key):
    return np.dot(query, key)  # already covered in the previous two topics for direct comparison

additive_score = additive_attention_score(query, key, W_combine, v_score)
dotproduct_score = dot_product_score(query, key)

print(f"Additive Attention score: {additive_score:.4f}")
print(f"Dot-Product Attention score (already covered in earlier topics): {dotproduct_score:.4f}")
print("\nAdditive Attention required its own genuinely additional learned weights, already covered as this topic's own core tradeoff")

blocks.text: 11. Key Takeaways

items: Additive Attention computes relevance scores by summing Query and Key, then a small learned network.
This differs from Dot-Product Attention, which multiplies Query and Key directly.
A small, dedicated fully connected layer, typically using Tanh, produces the final score.
It requires its own additional learned weights beyond the Query, Key, Value projections.
A learned, non-linear scoring function can in principle capture richer relationships.
It costs more computation than the simple dot product used in Scaled Dot-Product Attention.
This computational cost is a real, practical reason Scaled Dot-Product Attention became the standard default.
It can still be a reasonable choice for lower-dimensional vectors, where the extra cost matters less.
Next up: Self-Attention, applying these scoring approaches within a single sequence rather than between two.
